questions.q: What is a key weakness of a basic bag-of-words sentiment approach?
options: It requires a GPU to run at all
It ignores word order and context, so phrases can be scored incorrectly based on isolated word matches
It can only be applied to numerical data
It cannot process English text
questions.explain: Bag-of-words counts word occurrences against a list without regard for grammar, order, or context, so it can misjudge sentiment in phrases where word placement changes the meaning.

questions.q: What problem does the Loughran-McDonald lexicon specifically address?
options: It speeds up transformer model training
It translates financial text between languages
General-purpose sentiment dictionaries misclassify routine financial vocabulary (like 'liability' or 'tax') as negative
It removes the need for any timestamp on text data
questions.explain: The Loughran-McDonald lexicon was built from real financial disclosures specifically because general sentiment dictionaries tag ordinary financial terms as negative even though they're neutral, routine language in financial text.

questions.q: What distinguishes a FinBERT-style model from a basic bag-of-words approach?
options: It is a transformer-based model fine-tuned on financial text that captures context, rather than just counting words
It only works on non-English text
It cannot be used for sentiment classification
It requires no training data of any kind
questions.explain: FinBERT is a BERT-family model fine-tuned specifically on financial communications, allowing it to capture context and word relationships that bag-of-words approaches discard entirely.

questions.q: What is the text-specific version of the leakage problem discussed in this lesson?
options: Using more than one lexicon at a time
Timestamping a text-derived feature to when the event happened or the period it covers, rather than when the information actually became public
Running a model on too much text data
Using sentiment scores from more than one stock at once
questions.explain: If a filing-derived feature is timestamped to the fiscal period it covers rather than its actual release date, or an earnings-call feature is dated to the start of the trading day rather than after the call ends, the model is handed information before it was really available.

questions.q: Why does the lesson caution that text-derived sentiment signals remain noisy even when timing and modeling are done correctly?
options: Because sentiment is always exactly priced into the market one day later
Because transformer models always produce random output
Because sentiment is a proxy for market-moving information, not the information itself, and may already be priced in or misread by the market
Because text data cannot be timestamped at all
questions.explain: Sentiment extracted from news or filings only proxies for actual market-moving information; the same content can be already priced in, misinterpreted, or simply irrelevant, so text-derived features need the same importance and stability checks as any other feature.
